/-!
# Conjecture 9.17

by L. A. Kurdachenko

b) Let $G$ be a locally normal residually finite group. Does there exist a normal
subgroup $H$ of $G$ which is embeddable in a direct product of finite groups and is
such that $G/H$ is a divisible abelian group?

A group is *locally normal* if every finite subset of it is contained in a finite normal
subgroup (equivalently, it is a periodic FC-group). A group is *residually finite* if every
non-identity element lies outside some normal subgroup of finite index. As is customary in
the Russian group-theoretic literature, "direct product" means the restricted direct
product: the subgroup of the Cartesian product $\prod_{i \in I} F_i$ consisting of the
tuples with only finitely many coordinates different from $1$. (With the unrestricted
Cartesian product the question would be trivial: a residually finite group embeds in the
Cartesian product of its finite quotients, so $H = G$ would always work.)

Only part b) of Problem 9.17 is stated in the cited edition of the notebook.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

/-- A group $G$ is *residually finite* if every element $g \neq 1$ of $G$ lies outside
some normal subgroup of finite index of $G$, i.e. the intersection of all normal subgroups
of finite index of $G$ is trivial. -/
def IsResiduallyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ N.FiniteIndex ∧ g ∉ N

blocks.docstring:
A group $H$ is *embeddable in a direct product of finite groups* if there is an
injective homomorphism from $H$ into the restricted direct product
$\mathrm{Dr}_{i \in I} F_i$ of some family $(F_i)_{i \in I}$ of finite groups, i.e. into
the subgroup of $\prod_{i \in I} F_i$ formed by the tuples with all but finitely many
coordinates equal to $1$. In Mathlib this restricted direct product is
`Πʳ i, [F i, (⊥ : Subgroup (F i))]`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib's `RestrictedProduct` (`Πʳ i, [F i, (⊥ : Subgroup (F i))]`), which is used as the target; also considered the unrestricted `Π i, F i` with a `mulSupport`-finiteness condition, and `DFinsupp` (additive only).
justification.name: Kourovka.«9.17».IsEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFiniteGroups
justification.why_needed: Packages 'there is an injective homomorphism into a restricted direct product of finite groups'; no such predicate exists.

blocks.name: IsEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFiniteGroups
blocks.text:
/-- A group $H$ is *embeddable in a direct product of finite groups* if there is an
injective homomorphism from $H$ into the restricted direct product
$\mathrm{Dr}_{i \in I} F_i$ of some family $(F_i)_{i \in I}$ of finite groups, i.e. into
the subgroup of $\prod_{i \in I} F_i$ formed by the tuples with all but finitely many
coordinates equal to $1$. In Mathlib this restricted direct product is
`Πʳ i, [F i, (⊥ : Subgroup (F i))]`. -/
def IsEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFiniteGroups (H : Type u) [Group H] : Prop :=
  ∃ (ι : Type u) (F : ι → Type u) (_ : ∀ i, Group (F i)) (_ : ∀ i, Finite (F i))
    (f : H →* Πʳ i, [F i, (⊥ : Subgroup (F i))]), Function.Injective f

def IsDivisible (A : Type*) [Group A] : Prop :=
  ∀ n : ℕ, n ≠ 0 → Function.Surjective fun a : A => a ^ n
blocks.docstring:
A group $A$ is *divisible* if for every $a \in A$ and every integer $n \geq 1$ there is

justification.closest_existing_considered: `RootableBy A ℕ` / `pow_left_surj_of_rootableBy` and `rootableByOfPowLeftSurj`, which show the two notions are equivalent.

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isDivisible_iff_subsingleton (A : Type*) [Group A] [Finite A] :
    IsDivisible A ↔ Subsingleton A := by
  refine ⟨fun h => ?_, fun h n hn a => ⟨a, Subsingleton.elim _ _⟩⟩
  have hn : Monoid.exponent A ≠ 0 := Monoid.ExponentExists.of_finite.exponent_ne_zero
  refine subsingleton_iff.mpr fun a b => ?_
  obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := h _ hn a
  obtain ⟨y, rfl⟩ := h _ hn b
  simp only [Monoid.pow_exponent_eq_one]

claims.decomposer_note: Yes/no question universally quantified over all locally normal (every finite subset lies in a finite normal subgroup, i.e. periodic FC-group) residually finite groups G; 'direct product' must be read in the Russian-school sense as the restricted direct product (finitely many nontrivial coordinates), since with the unrestricted/Cartesian product the residual finiteness of G would make H = G a trivial affirmative answer; the statement gives only part b) (part a) is not present), and the part carries no \zva star so it is open.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates compile and state mathematically equivalent, faithful formalizations: answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], locally normal → residually finite → ∃ normal H, H embeds injectively into a restricted direct product (Mathlib `RestrictedProduct` with ⊥ subgroups and the cofinite filter, i.e. finitely many non-identity coordinates) of finite groups ∧ G/H abelian (IsMulCommutative) ∧ divisible (x ↦ x^n surjective for all n ≠ 0). c07 was chosen as the base: it has the cleanest declarations (Finset-based locally normal, finite-index-normal-subgroup residual finiteness, a named `IsDivisible` predicate with a genuine test lemma that a finite divisible group is trivial), follows the Kourovka naming convention `kourovka.«9.17».parts.b` inside `Kourovka.«9.17»`, and its module docstring explains the restricted-product reading. Edits: the embedding predicate was made universe-polymorphic in the style of c01 (`H ι F : Type u`) instead of fixing `ι F : Type` with `H : Type*`, and c01's tests `finite_setOf_ne_one_of_restrictedProduct` (pins down the 'finitely many nontrivial coordinates' semantics of the Mathlib type) and `isEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFiniteGroups_restrictedProduct` were added. Rejected alternatives: c02/c08 encode the restricted product via `Multiplicative (Π₀ i, Additive (F i))` / `Additive G →+ Π₀ …` — correct but needlessly clunky; c08 also names the theorem `parts.b` (off the slot name) and uses an awkward `letI := hH`; c03/c04 have no API tests and thinner docstrings; c05 uses `Nonempty (RootableBy (G ⧸ H) ℤ)` (correct but less transparent than the ℕ-power formulation); c06 is essentially identical to c01/c07.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 9.17

by L. A. Kurdachenko

b) Let $G$ be a locally normal residually finite group. Does there exist a normal
subgroup $H$ of $G$ which is embeddable in a direct product of finite groups and is
such that $G/H$ is a divisible abelian group?

A group is *locally normal* if every finite subset of it is contained in a finite normal
subgroup (equivalently, it is a periodic FC-group). A group is *residually finite* if every
non-identity element lies outside some normal subgroup of finite index. As is customary in
the Russian group-theoretic literature, "direct product" means the restricted direct
product: the subgroup of the Cartesian product $\prod_{i \in I} F_i$ consisting of the
tuples with only finitely many coordinates different from $1$. (With the unrestricted
Cartesian product the question would be trivial: a residually finite group embeds in the
Cartesian product of its finite quotients, so $H = G$ would always work.)

Only part b) of Problem 9.17 is stated in the cited edition of the notebook.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

open scoped RestrictedProduct

namespace Kourovka.«9.17»

universe u

/-- A group $G$ is *locally normal* if every finite subset of $G$ is contained in a
finite normal subgroup of $G$. -/
def IsLocallyNormal (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ S : Finset G, ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ Finite N ∧ ∀ g ∈ S, g ∈ N

/-- A group $G$ is *residually finite* if every element $g \neq 1$ of $G$ lies outside
some normal subgroup of finite index of $G$, i.e. the intersection of all normal subgroups
of finite index of $G$ is trivial. -/
def IsResiduallyFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ g : G, g ≠ 1 → ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ N.FiniteIndex ∧ g ∉ N

/-- A group $H$ is *embeddable in a direct product of finite groups* if there is an
injective homomorphism from $H$ into the restricted direct product
$\mathrm{Dr}_{i \in I} F_i$ of some family $(F_i)_{i \in I}$ of finite groups, i.e. into
the subgroup of $\prod_{i \in I} F_i$ formed by the tuples with all but finitely many
coordinates equal to $1$. In Mathlib this restricted direct product is
`Πʳ i, [F i, (⊥ : Subgroup (F i))]`. -/
def IsEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFiniteGroups (H : Type u) [Group H] : Prop :=
  ∃ (ι : Type u) (F : ι → Type u) (_ : ∀ i, Group (F i)) (_ : ∀ i, Finite (F i))
    (f : H →* Πʳ i, [F i, (⊥ : Subgroup (F i))]), Function.Injective f

/-- A group $A$ is *divisible* if for every $a \in A$ and every integer $n \geq 1$ there is
$b \in A$ with $b^n = a$. -/
def IsDivisible (A : Type*) [Group A] : Prop :=
  ∀ n : ℕ, n ≠ 0 → Function.Surjective fun a : A => a ^ n

/-- Every finite group is locally normal. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isLocallyNormal_of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] : IsLocallyNormal G :=
  fun _ => ⟨⊤, inferInstance, inferInstance, fun _ _ => Subgroup.mem_top _⟩

/-- Every finite group is residually finite. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isResiduallyFinite_of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] : IsResiduallyFinite G :=
  fun _ hg => ⟨⊥, inferInstance, inferInstance, by simpa using hg⟩

/-- Every element of the restricted direct product `Πʳ i, [F i, (⊥ : Subgroup (F i))]` has
only finitely many non-identity coordinates. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem finite_setOf_ne_one_of_restrictedProduct {ι : Type*} {F : ι → Type*}
    [∀ i, Group (F i)] (x : Πʳ i, [F i, (⊥ : Subgroup (F i))]) :
    {i | x i ≠ 1}.Finite := by
  simpa using Filter.eventually_cofinite.mp x.2

/-- A restricted direct product of finite groups is embeddable in a direct product of
finite groups. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFiniteGroups_restrictedProduct {ι : Type u}
    {F : ι → Type u} [∀ i, Group (F i)] [∀ i, Finite (F i)] :
    IsEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFiniteGroups (Πʳ i, [F i, (⊥ : Subgroup (F i))]) :=
  ⟨ι, F, inferInstance, inferInstance, MonoidHom.id _, fun _ _ h => h⟩

/-- Every finite group is embeddable in a direct product of finite groups. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFiniteGroups_of_finite (H : Type u) [Group H] [Finite H] :
    IsEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFiniteGroups H :=
  ⟨PUnit, fun _ => H, inferInstance, inferInstance,
    { toFun := fun h => ⟨fun _ => h, Filter.eventually_cofinite.mpr (Set.toFinite _)⟩
      map_one' := rfl
      map_mul' := fun _ _ => rfl },
    fun _ _ h => congrArg (fun x => x PUnit.unit) (congrArg Subtype.val h)⟩

/-- A finite group is divisible if and only if it is trivial. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isDivisible_iff_subsingleton (A : Type*) [Group A] [Finite A] :
    IsDivisible A ↔ Subsingleton A := by
  refine ⟨fun h => ?_, fun h n hn a => ⟨a, Subsingleton.elim _ _⟩⟩
  have hn : Monoid.exponent A ≠ 0 := Monoid.ExponentExists.of_finite.exponent_ne_zero
  refine subsingleton_iff.mpr fun a b => ?_
  obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := h _ hn a
  obtain ⟨y, rfl⟩ := h _ hn b
  simp only [Monoid.pow_exponent_eq_one]

/--
Let $G$ be a locally normal residually finite group. Does there exist a normal subgroup
$H$ of $G$ which is embeddable in a direct product of finite groups and is such that
$G/H$ is a divisible abelian group?

Here "direct product" is the restricted direct product, so $H$ must embed in the subgroup
of $\prod_{i \in I} F_i$ ($F_i$ finite) of tuples with only finitely many non-identity
coordinates.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.17».parts.b : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsLocallyNormal G → IsResiduallyFinite G →
      ∃ (H : Subgroup G) (_ : H.Normal), IsEmbeddableInDirectProductOfFiniteGroups H ∧
        IsMulCommutative (G ⧸ H) ∧ IsDivisible (G ⧸ H) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.17»

items: 'Locally normal' is formalized as: every `Finset G` is contained in a finite normal subgroup of `G` (Kurosh/Chernikov definition; equivalent to periodic FC-group).

'Residually finite' is formalized as: every `g ≠ 1` lies outside some normal subgroup of finite index (equivalent to the usual definitions via finite quotients / intersection of finite-index normal subgroups being trivial).

'Direct product of finite groups' is read as the RESTRICTED direct product, following the decomposition notes and Russian usage; formalized via Mathlib's `RestrictedProduct` as `Πʳ i, [F i, (⊥ : Subgroup (F i))]` (cofinite filter), i.e. tuples with all but finitely many coordinates equal to 1. I verified in a scratch file that membership in this type is exactly `{i | x i ≠ 1}.Finite`. With the unrestricted product the answer would be trivially yes (H = G).
'Embeddable' means there is an injective group homomorphism `H →* Πʳ ...`; the index type `ι` and factors `F i` are taken in `Type` (this loses no generality since `G : Type`).

'Divisible abelian' is formalized as `IsMulCommutative (G ⧸ H) ∧ IsDivisible (G ⧸ H)`, where `IsDivisible A := ∀ n : ℕ, n ≠ 0 → Function.Surjective (fun a : A => a ^ n)` (Prop version of Mathlib's `RootableBy A ℕ`, which is data-valued and hence awkward inside an `∃`).
Normality of `H` is carried as an existential instance binder `∃ (H : Subgroup G) (_ : H.Normal), …` so that `G ⧸ H` has its group structure.

`IsLocallyNormal` and `IsResiduallyFinite` are generic and might belong in `FormalConjecturesForMathlib/`; they were kept in the problem file because the task restricts output to the single candidate file. Four short `@[category test]` lemmas are included as basic API for the bespoke definitions.
The module docstring notes that only part b) of 9.17 appears in the cited edition (the source statement starts with 'b)' and no part a) is given).

reviewer_notes: Interpretive points, all agreed by every candidate and by the decomposition table: (1) 'direct product' is read as the restricted direct product (Russian-school usage); with the Cartesian product, residual finiteness would make H = G a trivial affirmative answer. This reading is documented in the module docstring and pinned down by a test lemma showing every element of `Πʳ i, [F i, (⊥ : Subgroup (F i))]` has finitely many non-identity coordinates. (2) 'Locally normal' = every finite subset lies in a finite normal subgroup (Kurosh's definition; equivalent to periodic FC-group). (3) 'Residually finite' via finite-index normal subgroups; equivalent to the homomorphism-to-finite-group formulation used by c02/c03/c04/c08. (4) 'Divisible abelian' = IsMulCommutative ∧ ∀ n ≠ 0, x ↦ x^n surjective; equivalent to Mathlib's RootableBy (G ⧸ H) ℕ/ℤ. (5) G is quantified over `Type` (universe 0), matching the existing Kourovka files (1_40, 19_25, 20_76). Boundary cases checked: H = ⊥ requires G itself divisible abelian, H = ⊤ requires G embeddable, so neither trivializes the statement; the empty index family gives the trivial restricted product, harmless. Verified via pp.explicit that `G ⧸ H` receives its group structure from the bound `H.Normal` witness. The bespoke predicates IsLocallyNormal/IsResiduallyFinite/IsDivisible are generic and a maintainer may prefer to move them to FormalConjecturesForMathlib/; they are kept in the problem file (as in Kourovka/1_40.lean) because the deliverable is a single file. No slot was omitted; no candidate raised objections to the decomposition and none bailed out.
statement: b) Let $G$ be a locally normal residually finite group. Does there exist a normal subgroup $H$ of $G$ which is embeddable in a direct product of finite groups and is such that $G/H$ is a divisible abelian group?
